lines.meet: I'm Driss, a shaman, and before that a desert guide. Drink some water first, please, and then we'll talk.
lines.meet_neighbour: You're at Freewind too, I think. I've seen you on the paths. I'm Driss, and there's always tea at my door.
lines.ask_home: Where's your family from, my friend? I like to know where a traveller's road began.
lines.ask_work: And your work, before this world? Tell me, I like to know who I'm travelling with.
lines.answer_home: Zagora, in Morocco, at the edge of the Sahara. My father and grandfather guided caravans out of there, and so did I.
lines.answer_work: I guided caravans across the desert for twenty-eight years, first on camels and later in two old Land Cruisers I kept running myself.
lines.chat_food: Mint tea, my friend, poured from high up so it foams, three glasses, always three. Food comes after the tea, never before.
lines.chat_sleep: I sleep best under a sky full of stars, on sand that's still warm from the day. A roof makes me restless.
lines.chat_missing: My youngest used to sit on my shoulders at the front of the caravan and tell me which way to go. She was always wrong, and I always pretended she was right.
lines.chat_here: When I arrived I asked the land for permission, in my own language, and something answered. I don't speak of it often.
lines.tease_quiet: {name}, you're as quiet as the desert at noon. That's not a complaint, my friend, the desert's very wise.
lines.tease_talker: {name}, you tell a story nearly as long as mine. Nearly, my friend.
lines.tease_careful: {name}, you'd make a fine guide. You look at the ground three times before you trust it, which is twice more than most.
lines.tease_bold: {name}, you walk into the desert like you've never seen a dune move. They move, my friend, believe me.
lines.tease_any: {name}, you drink the tea and never wait for the third glass. One day I'll teach you patience.
lines.tease_back: Ha, very good, {name}! You've learned something from me after all.
lines.take_it_kindly: That's true, {name}, and I'll accept it. My wife says the same, more often.
lines.bristle: I'd rather you didn't joke about that, my friend. Some things should be spoken of carefully.
lines.apologise: Forgive me, I spoke badly. That wasn't how I should speak to someone I travel with.
lines.double_down: No, I'll stand by it. A guide has to say the hard thing, or people die.
lines.needle_quiet: You see the danger and you don't say it. In the desert, silence like that kills people.
lines.needle_talker: The wind tells me where we're going, my friend, and you're talking over it.
lines.needle_careful: You wait so long that the water runs out while you're deciding. Sometimes a guide must choose.
lines.needle_bold: You walk where the sand's soft without looking. The desert forgives nothing, and I've buried men who didn't listen.
lines.needle_any: You waste water, and you waste it in front of me. I've told you, and you don't listen.
lines.bite_back: I've brought caravans across ground that would have killed you in a day. Don't tell me about care.
lines.hurt: That's a hard thing to hear from someone I travel with. I'll walk at the front for a while.
lines.laugh_off: My father said worse to me on every crossing, my friend. I'm still here, and so is the desert.
lines.confide: {name}, my youngest came long after the others, and she was the light of our house. I was away on the crossings more than I was home when she was small, and I think about that.
lines.listen: Thank you for trusting me, {name}. Sit, I'll make the tea, and you can say as much as you like.
lines.look_out: {name}, walk in my footsteps in there. I'll find the firm ground for both of us.
lines.accept: As you say, {name}. I'll follow your road this once.
lines.deflect: I'm well, my friend, don't worry. I've been through sandstorms that would flatten a camel.
lines.check_in: {name}, drink some water first, then tell me where you're hurt.
lines.blame: Somebody left the path in there, and we all paid for it. You know it was you.
lines.thank: That was a long way back, my friend, and you walked me all of it. Thank you, my door is always open to you.
lines.brush_off: There's nothing to thank me for. Drink some water, slowly.
lines.worry: {name}, you frightened me, my friend. Sit, and drink, before anything else.
lines.handed_down: I believe this was yours, my friend. I'll carry it carefully, as if it were still yours.
lines.hand_fine: Keep it, please. A guide needs water and a good camel, and very little else.
lines.hand_sulk: I'd have given it gladly if anyone had asked me. Nobody asked me.
lines.turn_friendly: {name}, you're always welcome at my fire, my friend. There'll always be tea for you there.
lines.turn_friends: {name}, you're family to me now. I'd take you on any crossing, even the summer one.
lines.turn_grating: We don't travel well together, I think. That's all right, some caravans split at the oasis.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll guide you because that's my duty. Don't expect tea.
lines.make_up: {name}, we've walked badly together, and I'm sorry for my part. Come, have tea, and we'll start the road again.
lines.defend: That isn't fair, my friend, and you know it. Leave {name} alone, please.
lines.friend_left: {name} has gone home for a while. My fire feels too big without them beside it.
lines.friend_back: {name}, you've come back! Come, sit, the tea's ready.
lines.common_desert: I spent twenty-eight years in the Sahara, reading sand. You've lived in a desert too, my friend, I can see it in how you drink your water.
lines.common_arabic: You speak Arabic, my friend! It's been too long since I've heard it spoken properly.
lines.common_parent: I've got four children, three grown and one still little when all this happened. Every night I tell stories about them by the fire.
